User Profile ​

The signed-in user's profile is a JSON object, available as await skapi.user and from getProfile().

Updating the profile ​

updateProfile(_:) changes the signed-in user's own profile and returns the updated profile.

swift
import Skapi

let skapi = try Skapi(projectId: "<Project ID>")
try await skapi.login(email: "user@example.com", password: "password")

let user = try await skapi.updateProfile(["name": "Ana", "nickname": "ana"])
print(user["name"]?.string ?? "")  // Ana

Pass only the fields you want to change. An empty string "" clears a field:

swift
try await skapi.updateProfile(["nickname": ""])

email cannot be cleared. A changed e-mail becomes unverified until the user verifies it.

Keys that are not profile fields are ignored. Anonymous accounts cannot edit their profile.

Profile fields ​

Fields the user can set, at signup or with updateProfile(_:):

fieldvalue
emailthe user's e-mail
name, nickname, given_name, middle_name, family_nametext
gendertext, for example "female" or "male"
birthdate"yyyy-mm-dd"
phone_number"+" and digits, for example "+821012345678"
addresstext, or an object such as ["formatted": ..., "locality": ..., "region": ..., "postal_code": ..., "country": ...]
picture, profile, websitea full URL
miscany text for your own use; only the user and admins can read it

Fields set by Skapi, which the user cannot change:

fieldvalue
user_idthe user's ID
service, ownerthe project and its owner
access_groupthe account's access level, a number
approved"{approver}:{approved or suspended}:{timestamp}"
localecountry code where the user signed up
loglast login time, in seconds
email_verifiedtrue when the e-mail is verified
anonymoustrue on anonymous accounts, absent otherwise

Public fields ​

email, phone_number, address, gender and birthdate are private by default. Set the matching *_public flag to true to let other users see that field when they search users.

swift
try await skapi.updateProfile(["gender": "female", "gender_public": true])

The flags are email_public, phone_number_public, address_public, gender_public and birthdate_public, and must be true or false. A flag appears in the profile only when its field is set. email_public: true needs a verified e-mail, or it throws INVALID_REQUEST.

Disabling an account ​

A user who leaves your project can disable their own account with disableAccount(). They are logged out at once, and all data of the account is deleted after 90 days.

swift
print(try await skapi.disableAccount().string ?? "")  // SUCCESS: account has been disabled.

Recovering a disabled account ​

Within those 90 days, logging in to a disabled account throws USER_IS_DISABLED. Call recoverAccount(redirect:) on the same Skapi object to send the user an e-mail with a recovery link. Opening the link reactivates the account.

swift
do {
    try await skapi.login(email: "user@example.com", password: "password")
} catch let err as SkapiError where err.code == "USER_IS_DISABLED" {
    print(try await skapi.recoverAccount())  // SUCCESS: Recovery e-mail has been sent.
}

Pass a full URL, recoverAccount(redirect: "https://your.site/welcome-back"), to have the link lead there after the recovery. The account can only be recovered when its e-mail is verified and the user knows their password.
